History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
- 47-year-old woman with 2-week progressive numbness/tingling and weakness of the left upper limb and a prior brief episode of left-eye visual loss; urgent neurology referral arranged to rule out demyelinating disease (e.g., multiple sclerosis).

History:
- Chief complaint: Numbness, tingling, and perceived weakness of the left arm.
- Onset/duration: Began ≈2 weeks ago after starting a boxing class; symptoms have progressively worsened.
- Character/progression:
  • Tingling initially mild, now accompanied by numbness from elbow to hand.  
  • Affects palmar aspect of 2nd–4th digits; present at rest.  
  • Reports difficulty with fine motor tasks (playing piano) but can still grasp objects with dominant right hand.  
  • Occasional left shoulder discomfort during boxing movements.  
- Relieving/aggravating factors: Massage and warm baths ineffective; ibuprofen taken for unrelated right-hand knuckle pain with no change in numbness.
- Associated/other symptoms:
  • Transient monocular visual disturbance: ~20-minute loss of part of visual field in left eye a few weeks ago, resolved spontaneously.  
  • Occasional “tired” headaches and fatigue.  
  • Recent severe upper-respiratory illness lasting ~2 weeks one month ago.  
  • Denies seizures, loss of consciousness, lower-limb weakness; gait normal.
- Review of systems (pertinent negatives/positives):
  • Vision: transient deficit as above; no ongoing blurring.  
  • Neurological: no fits/seizures; no lower-limb symptoms.  
  • Neck pain: patient initially said “yes” then recanted (“no, nothing”) – conflict noted.  
  • No mention of bowel/bladder dysfunction, speech difficulty, or facial weakness.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical conditions reported.
- History of iron deficiency suspected by PCP (takes supplements intermittently).

Medications:
- Ibuprofen as needed (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
- Vitamin D (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
- Iron supplements intermittently (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
- Melatonin as needed for sleep (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Allergies:
- Not documented.

Social History:
- Physically active; attends boxing classes for past few weeks.  
- Alcohol: occasional; describes one recent episode of heavy drinking.  
- Smoking and illicit substance use: not discussed.  
- Occupation and living situation: not discussed.

Family History:
- Father: hypothyroidism and other unspecified autoimmune condition.  
- Mother: type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia.  
- No known family history of neurological disorders.

Physical Examination:
- Tele-consult; no vitals or physical findings documented.

Investigations:
- None to date.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Left upper-limb numbness/weakness with sensory involvement (palmar 2nd–4th digits) and prior transient visual loss.
  - Assessment: Possible demyelinating disease (e.g., multiple sclerosis) versus peripheral neuropathy/cervical radiculopathy from boxing.  
  - Plan:  
    • Arrange urgent neurology referral for further assessment.  
    • Anticipate brain MRI ± spinal imaging and formal neurological examination.  
    • No disease-specific therapy initiated pending diagnosis.  
    • Provide red-flag advice: attend Emergency Department if weakness progresses to legs, if new severe headaches, vomiting, seizures, or persistent/worsening visual symptoms develop.

General Plan items:
- Continue current analgesia (ibuprofen) for unrelated musculoskeletal pain as needed.  
- Encourage avoidance of aggravating boxing activities until evaluated.  
- Ensure adequate rest and hydration.  
- Follow up after neurology evaluation or sooner if symptoms change.

Quality checks:

• Missing but clinically expected elements:
  – Allergies not obtained.  
  – Complete medication list with doses/frequencies.  
  – Vitals, focused neurological examination, and smoking history absent.  

• Internal conflicts:
  – Patient both affirmed and denied neck pain in the same response (“Yes, absolutely… no, nothing”) – conflict noted.

• Transcript quality:
  – Clear overall; minor conversational overlaps and pauses but clinically usable.
